- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to revert; apply a mild downward bias in next 5-7 days to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates the upside; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior 7-day average.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often exhibits lag — forecast is 1–3 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.  
- If model consistently underpredicts true price in the 2nd–3rd week of forecast horizon, apply a 0.8–1.2% upward adjustment to compensate for lagged momentum.  
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps sharply but price remains flat, model often overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in next 3 days.
